children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a weak opening on November 18, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is trading lower at 25,304.50 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

Indian benchmark indices extended their winning streak for a second consecutive session on November 17, with the Nifty reclaiming the 25,500 mark intraday for the first time since February 2026, led by gains in auto, banking and realty stocks.
At close, the Sensex was up 427.40 points or 0.52 percent at 82,532.19, and the Nifty was up 96.30 points or 0.38 percent at 25,387.40.
Biggest Nifty gainers were M&M, Axis Bank, Eicher Motors, Asian Paints, Interglobe Aviation, while losers included HCL Technologies, Power Grid Corp, Coal India, HDFC Life and Infosys.
Among sectors, the IT index shed 0.9%, and the FMCG index fell 0.3%, while Realty and PSU Bank indices rose nearly 2% each; media, metal, oil & gas, auto, private bank, and infra were up 0.5-0.9%.
The broader indices ended mixed, with the Nifty midcap index rising 0.3 percent, while the smallcap index fell 0.22 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Down)
GIFT Nifty was trading weak at around 25,304.50 in early trade, indicating a negative opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Gain)
Asian shares were trading mostly higher in the early trade on Wednesday, with South Korea's tech-heavy KOSPI jumping 1.6%, while Japan's Nikkei added 0.4%.
US Equities (Down)

A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on Monday as ​fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO soured enthusiasm for AI stocks, raising the stakes for the chipmaker's earnings report ‌on Tuesday and Anthropic's initial public offering later in the week.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17, the S&P 500 lost 145.08 points, or 1.92%, to 7,416.59 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 626.51 points, or 2.49%, to 24,509.76.
Dollar Index (Up)
The dollar held steady near a 19-month high on Wednesday as US economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials lent support to the case for interest rate hikes.

The yen edged lower even after Japanese trade figures showed exports set a record monthly value in October on strong demand in the semiconductor sector. The Aussie dollar languished near a 10-month low.
US Bond Yield (Up)
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasury bonds were up marginally at 5.11% and 4.81%, respectively, in the early trade on Wednesday.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar on Wednesday, with the Indonesian rupiah emerging as the top gainer, rising 0.066 percent from its previous close. The South Korean won gained 0.315 percent, while the Philippine peso and Taiwan dollar edged up 0.053 percent and 0.003 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Japanese yen declined 0.138 percent, recording the biggest loss among regional peers, followed by the Thai baht, which slipped 0.044 percent. The Singapore dollar, Chinese renminbi and Malaysian ringgit also weakened marginally by 0.031 percent, 0.026 percent and 0.024 percent, respectively
Crude (Down)
Oil steadied as traders assessed renewed fighting in the Middle East against signs of recovering supplies and higher US inventories.
Brent held near $93 a barrel after swinging in a near-$3 range on Tuesday, while West Texas Intermediate was above $85.
Gold (Down)
Gold was steady near a 14-month low, after Federal Reserve officials argued the case for more rate hikes to tackle stubborn inflation.
Bullion was near $3,850 an ounce, after dipping 0.2% on Tuesday to its lowest close since September 2025.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued their buying streak for the sixth consecutive session on November 17, purchasing equities worth Rs 4,195 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) snapped their 12-day selling streak, turning net buyers with equity purchases worth Rs 196 crore.
